title: What is India's Industrial Production Index (IIP) and Why Did It Get an Update?
description: India's factory output, measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 4.9% in April 2026. The government has updated how it calculates IIP, us.

faq.q: What does a 4.9% IIP growth mean?
faq.a: It means that the total industrial output in April 2026 was 4.9% higher than what it was in April 2025, according to the new measurement system.

faq.q: How often is IIP data released?
faq.a: IIP data is usually released every month by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

faq.q: Why is 2022-23 chosen as the new base year?
faq.a: A base year is typically chosen to be a "normal" year, free from major economic shocks, and one for which comprehensive data is available. It also needs to be updated periodically to reflect structural changes in the economy.

faq.q: Does the new base year affect past IIP numbers?
faq.a: Yes, when a new base year is introduced, historical IIP data is often re-calculated using the new base year to allow for consistent comparison over time. However, the focus is usually on the new series for future and recent comparisons.

faq.q: Is a higher IIP always good?
faq.a: Generally, yes. A higher IIP indicates increased production, which often translates to economic growth, job creation, and improved supply of goods. However, extremely rapid, unsustainable growth could sometimes lead to other issues like inflation, though that's a broader economic concern.
